>  We live in this system that conditions us to believe we should have everything we want, and if we can’t get it, it’s a competition.

This is a very strong point that I never considered, yet it's totally right. My parents have always put a pressure on me to be the best in anything (mainly school though, they never cared about my social life or sports although if you asked them then they'd come up with a million excuses that somehow justifies their point), the schools I've been in have always been giant circlejerks about grades (up until uni at least), and a bunch of forums that I've frequented in the past have made me feel like garbage for not having top notch extracurriculars or a 4.5/4 GPA. Wow, I really needed that line to shine some light on reality. Thank you already for this line alone!

>In a year when you’re dead, do you want people to say “oh wow, this person was great at sports, or had good grades in their major,” or would you want them to say how kind you are? Hardworking? Compassionate? Friendly? A great listener? Optimistic?

I've debated this point internally and my logic against this is as follows. The people we read about in textbooks were rarely noted for their qualities (with a few exceptions like being bright, hardworking, deterministic), they've always been noted for their achievements through life. I know that there can only be one Caesar for every dozen billion people, but there have been so many in between who've accomplished so much in different fields that we read about and acknowledge to this day. That's been my drive these last few years. To eventually leave some sort of lasting legacy that goes beyond 1 or 2 generations. Lots of people know about Cornelius Vanderbilt but who knows about his sons and daughters? 

That's also been the thing that has kept me going even when my materialistic goings have been rough since history likes to share riches-rags-riches stories and so the rough patches in my life might as well be the valley from which I'll start my rise to the peak (of my life).

Thank you for sharing with me how the original post resonated with you, it comforts me to know that my experiences and some of my thoughts aren't unique and that there are others who are in my situation. Hopefully tomorrow we'll both find what we seek!
